reading.body:
The graph underlying this site contains 25,950 recorded edges across eleven relationship types, connecting models, companies, people, papers, patents, lawsuits, and regulatory filings into a single navigable structure.

The largest edge class by far is model-to-modality assignment, with 16,371 entries, followed by 8,659 model-to-paper citations derived from arXiv identifiers that model authors placed in their own Hub tags. Together those two classes account for roughly 97 percent of all edges, which means the graph is primarily a map of the model and research layer. The remaining nine relationship types, covering 332 products, 122 fundraising filings, 110 MCP server publishers, 108 patent holders, 72 lawsuit defendants, 37 SEC registrants, 28 vendor feeds, 12 monitored APIs, and 99 categorized people, are real but thin by comparison.

The citation edges are worth particular attention for readers tracking how knowledge moves into compute. When model authors tag their own work with arXiv identifiers, that is a direct, low-noise signal of which research a model builder considered close enough to claim. Eight thousand six hundred fifty-nine such links, extracted by the method described, form a traceable lineage from paper to deployed model. The legal and financial edges, drawn from CourtListener, SEC EDGAR, and the USPTO, add an institutional layer that the technical data alone cannot provide.

What the data does not cover is causation or weight. An edge records that a relationship exists and how it was detected, not how significant it is. The graph was generated on a single date, so it reflects the state of tracked sources on that day and will drift as filings, registries, and Hub tags change.
